what_this_is: Governed Phase-2 decisions: for a recurrence family, what the CURRENT primary authority says, what the present-day examinable core is, which answer a candidate should study today, and who independently reviewed that. Phase 1 says what recurs; this says what is true now.
what_this_is_not: Not a recurrence store. It never changes a family, an occurrence or a count. The pinned_at_selection block is a COPY taken at selection time so the validator can prove Phase 1 did not move underneath this work.
the_rule_that_governs_everything_here: MIW Written answers are SITTING-ANCHORED. Every answer must be true as at the date of its own examination sitting, not as at today (TEMPORAL_AND_DONOR_VERIFICATION_PROTOCOL s1). A model_answer may therefore be edited ONLY to fix something that was already wrong at its own sitting -- that is a CORRECTION. Where the framework moved AFTER the sitting, the answer is left alone and the present-day position is carried here, at family level, in present_day_position. That is a MODERNISATION. Collapsing the two would corrupt the past-paper product.

families.current_framework_finding: THE GOVERNING STATUTE HAS BEEN REPLACED ENTIRELY. Section 324(1) of the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 repeals the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 (except Part XIV, but not including section 411A therein) and the Coasting Vessels Act, 1838, with effect from 15 March 2026. present_day_provision_map.old: MS Act 1958 s.334 -- definition of unseaworthy ship
present_day_provision_map.note: Substantively the same test: materials, construction and design, number/description/qualification of seafarers including officers, weight/description/stowage of cargo and ballast, condition of hull, equipment, boilers and machinery, not such as to render her in every respect fit for the proposed voyage or service. present_day_provision_map.old: MS Act 1958 s.335 -- sending unseaworthy ship to sea
present_day_provision_map.new: MS Act 2025 s.127 -- "Unseaworthy vessel not to be sent to sea"
present_day_provision_map.note: s.127(1) the sender, s.127(2) the master who knowingly takes her to sea, each with the reasonable-and-justifiable defence; s.127(3) evidence. THE CHARACTER OF THE SANCTION HAS CHANGED: the 2025 Act casts these as liability to PENALTY rather than criminal offence.

present_day_provision_map.old: MS Act 1958 s.336 -- obligation of owner to crew as to seaworthiness
present_day_provision_map.new: MS Act 2025 s.128 -- "Obligation of ship owner, master or agent with respect to seaworthiness"
present_day_provision_map.note: s.128(1) implies into every contract of service, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary, an obligation to use all reasonable means to ensure seaworthiness at the commencement of the voyage and to keep her in a seaworthy state during it; s.128(2) survey power.

present_day_provision_map.new: MS Act 2025 s.278 and s.307, with s.308 for detention costs
present_day_provision_map.note: s.278 detention where a vessel arrives in or proceeds from an Indian port in an unseaworthy condition; s.307 control measures with an Explanation defining "unsafe vessel" as including an unseaworthy vessel which poses a risk to safety of life, or an unreasonable threat of harm to the environment by reason of safe manning, hull, machinery, equipment, training and working conditions or operational safety being substantially below required standards; appeal to the Director-General within seven days; s.308 makes the owner liable for detention costs.

present_day_provision_map.note: Unseaworthiness is deemed reasonable cause for desertion or absence without leave, PROVIDED the seafarer first complained to the master or a listed officer.

present_day_position: UNCLOS Articles 91, 92, 94 and 217 are unchanged. Article 94 duties of the flag State and Article 217 flag-State enforcement stand as stated.
The Indian implementing statute as at August 2026 is the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, in force from 15 March 2026.

The Indian maritime administration is the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (formerly DG Shipping); the office of Director-General of Maritime Administration is created by s.7(1) of the 2025 Act.
Registration of Indian vessels is governed by the 2025 Act (registration provisions at ss.15 to 17), not by the 1958 Act.
No authoritative test for the UNCLOS "genuine link" has been settled, and none should be offered.
